description: Hurricane Harvey Infrastructure Resilience Investigation is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Cheng-Chun Lee, Texas A&M University (tamu.edu). Hurricane Harvey, a Category 4 hurricane that hit the Texas coastline on August 25, 2017, is the most significant tropical cyclone rainfall event in the United States history since reliable records began around the 1880s. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-gcrf-h607. Keywords: Resilience, Hurricanes, Investigation. Published 2022-10-22. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
